item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00119","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C10","C01","C08"],"selected_candidate_label":"C10","confidence":0.96,"relationship_type":"literal_language_template","rationale":"C10 provides a close, compact drafting model for the child's central operative sentence: both begin in the first person with “I hereby delegate to the Secretary of State,” identify “the authority vested in the President” by specified legislation, and then describe the delegated subject. The child expands this same frame into two numbered authorities and adds revocation of an earlier directive. C01 and C08 use similar delegation-of-presidential-authority machinery, but their wording and structure are less directly aligned.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I hereby delegate to the Secretary of State (1) the authority vested in the President by section 3496 ... and (2) the authority vested in the President by section 3492(c)","parent_excerpt":"I hereby delegate to the Secretary of State and to any Assistant Secretary of State designated by him the authority vested in the President by Title V","explanation":"The distinctive first-person delegation formula, identical recipient, and statutory-authority frame closely match; the child adapts the singular delegation into a numbered pair."},{"child_excerpt":"the authority vested in the President ... to prescribe regulations","parent_excerpt":"the authority vested in the President ... relating to international children's welfare work","explanation":"Both sentences identify the delegated power by citing its statutory source and then specifying its substantive scope."}]}
